object: funerary stela with round top, fifteen lines, late transitional writing
site: Medik (from the filling of a pit grave cleared by Firth at Aqeba, January 1911), Lower Nubia
notes: Copy from Firth's photograph (Pls. VIII, IX). Griffith's translation: 'The honourable Wayekiye, truly beloved(?) of Shipeshiye and Qeresamaye, kin of Maleme the strategus, kin of Maqel-Teqaye the strategus in Bezewe, kin of Pakheme the great qeren, kin of Beke the Agent, kin of the shanapatete-cadet, kin of Matewawe the strategus of the azab ...'; then three more phrases, the invocation to Isis and Osiris (woSi : Soreyi) and formula G. His notes: l. 2, ':to' at the beginning is corrected outside the line to ':ye', and 'the first m [of mdemdeto] looks more like t'; l. 8 'Snptete' may contain the name of Napata; l. 9 Matewawe = Manitawawe of 97/5; l. 10 'penn', cf. 94/13, 29; l. 11 'the first character may be a numeral resembling that in 98/17, 101/8' (printed as the a-sign split in two, each half queried; counted here as one queried a); l. 13 the strokes '×IIII' are a numeral (regnal date or age?), written {×}{4}. In type line 12 the te is printed with a dot under its stroke (te or to?). The word yetmdelo broken across type lines 9-10 is kept whole. be(7)ke is joined across the line number after Griffith's 'Beke'; his translation also reads 'Qeresamaye' and 'qeren' as single words where the type prints qoresm ye and qore N.
